scope: 17 source records: primary studies, original method analyses, authoritative guidance and official provider documentation families. Not 17 validation trials.

sources.title: 2024 Adult Compendium: activity definitions and conventional METs
sources.populationAndWindow: Adults 19–59; target excludes conditions materially affecting metabolism.
sources.measurement: Standard MET convention; activity descriptions and measured/estimated entries.
sources.finding: Resistance categories differ by task and effort; they do not validate Metron’s complete 2.5/3.5/5 session mapping.
sources.limitations: Population averages, not individual calorimetry; older-adult and clinical transfer not established.
sources.inspectedPortions: Official adult overview, conditioning/walking tables; primary article indexed abstract and limitations. Full contributing studies not inspected.

sources.title: FAO/WHO/UNU: Human energy requirements
sources.populationAndWindow: Habitual adult daily activity patterns; 2001 consultation published 2004.
sources.measurement: PAL is 24-hour TEE divided by BMR.
sources.finding: Sedentary/light PAL category 1.40–1.69 uses a different numerator and denominator from Metron’s baseline component.
sources.limitations: Not evidence to substitute 1.4 for 1.2 or to certify the 2,000-step allowance.

sources.limitations: No universal adjustment factor for Metron, all workouts or clinical populations.

sources.title: Han et al.: Development of a Multivariable Equation for Predicting Healthy Step Length
sources.populationAndWindow: 252 healthy adults aged 18–90; repeated five-fold cross-validation within the same cohort.
sources.measurement: Multivariable step-length model including walking speed and stature.
sources.finding: Supports retaining gait conditions and model identity rather than treating height alone as an observation.
sources.limitations: Internal cross-validation is not independent validation; pathological gait and clinical outcomes not established.

sources.title: Scherrenberg et al.: smartphone six-minute walk assessment
sources.populationAndWindow: 102 cardiovascular patients enrolled in phase II cardiac rehabilitation; supervised study.
sources.measurement: Section 4.3 compares rounded height×0.413/0.415 step lengths with manually counted 30-m walking.
sources.finding: Reported step-length MAE 5.24 cm for the sex-specific formula comparison.
sources.limitations: Not the universal unrounded 0.415 rule, calorimetry or a Metron energy validation; main app tests used measured step length.

sources.title: Siedler et al.: reliability and validity of fifteen BIA devices
sources.populationAndWindow: 73 healthy adults aged 19–50; 37 returned after 12–16 weeks.

sources.finding: Device-specific validity differs from repeatability; near-identical retests warrant independence checks.
sources.limitations: Excluded major composition abnormalities and device-size limitations; no transferable SECA mBCA 515 calibration or universal error budget established.
